messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident 2026-03-14T20:00Z — high 429s observed for hosted-gpu-1 cluster. Queue growth on hotpath; autoscaler heartbeat missed. Paging oncall_lex. https://internal.incidents/1812468000

oncall_lex: I'm on it. grabbing context — what's the customer impact?

sanjay: seeing 15m tail of queued requests for model: gpt-mid-4x on hosted-gpu-1, p95 latency spiking to 12s and many 429s returned. Tokenbucket reject rate jumping ~8% over baseline.

maria: confirmed — metrics: GPU util ~98%, cluster pods at 100%, autoscaler logs show heartbeat lag (last heartbeat 00:17 ago). Not scheduling new nodes.

ops_nick: stacktrace from autoscaler: `ERROR: heartbeat monitor: lost lease to allocator, retrying` then `Failed to allocate pool: insufficient tiered capacity`. Looks like tier limits prevented scale-up.

oncall_lex: okay, initial plan: 1) mitigate customer impact (route to fallback model or enlarge pool), 2) stabilize autoscaler, 3) tune tokenbucket regen. Which is fastest?

lisa: fastest is to temporarily raise tokenbucket regen and fallback routing. If we increase regen, we reduce 429s from rate control but risk higher cost/overload.

ryan: I can flip fallback route to gpt-mid-4x-quantized (lower resource) for the highest-traffic routes. Prep command: `/deploy routing set-fallback --route hotpath --model gpt-mid-4x-quantized --duration 30m`

oncall_lex: do it. ryan, ping when done. I'll start increasing tokenbucket regen for the public tier from 200u/s -> 600u/s for 10m. Maria, can you patch that?

maria: applying tokenbucket change now (staging first then prod). Patch: ```yaml
ratepolicy:
  tiers:
    public:
      token_regen_per_sec: 600
      burst_capacity: 1200
```

maria: applied to prod route hotpath. Observability: token reject rate dropped from 8% -> 3% within 40s. GPU queue length still slowly decreasing.

ryan: routing change applied. fallback active for hotpath routes. Users on impacted endpoints now getting quantized variant. Quick check — latency p95 back to 3.2s down from 12s, 429s dropping.

oncall_lex: good. Now investigate why autoscaler heartbeat missed. Ops logs?

ops_nick: allocator locked up due to a leader election flapping in k8s control plane; autoscaler couldn't acquire tier lease. There's a race where tokenbucket throttles can deprioritize the allocator's control RPCs under heavy load. Essentially control RPCs got queued behind heavy hotpath work causing heartbeat misses.

sanjay: aha — we observed a deprioritization path: tokenbucket applies at edge for user requests and control plane traffic shares same worker thread pool, so control RPCs lose out. Need short-term: bump control priority and ensure allocator heartbeats are on a separate fast path.

lisa: short term mitigation: increase tokenbucket control priority weight and reduce client worker concurrency for hotpath. I can roll a config: `control_priority: high` and `client_worker_limit: 250` temporarily.

oncall_lex: do it, but coordinate with deploy-bot for config rollout.

deploy-bot: rolling config change to hosted-gpu-1: {control_priority: high, client_worker_limit: 250} — canary started

maria: canary 5% looks good, control heartbeats restored. Commencing full rollout.

ops_nick: autoscaler reacquired lease, started backfilling 2 additional nodes. Pool capacity increased, GPU util dropping to ~85%. Queue draining now.

oncall_lex: keep fallback routing in place for another 20m to be safe. Also keep tokenbucket regen elevated for 15m then step down. We'll revert in small steps and watch.

pm_zoe: customer impact — we're seeing elevated latency and 9% error budget burn for a handful of enterprise customers (acct IDs: acct-122, acct-987). Should we notify CS/AMs?

oncall_lex: yes, send a brief CS note: high latency and transient 429s affecting a subset; mitigations applied; ETA for full recovery ~30m. Lisa, can you draft?

lisa: drafting now: "We observed a capacity issue affecting some requests; we've applied fallback routing and autoscaler fixes. Expect normal service within 30–45 minutes. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."

oncall_lex: thanks. Ops — any permanent config work we should do now?

ops_nick: next actions (short list):
- separate control RPC worker pool so heartbeats can't be deprioritized by tokenbucket saturation
- add a low-latency fast-path for allocator leases
- add a circuit-breaker to avoid tokenbucket changes that temporarily starve control traffic
- tighten tier capacity limits vs autoscaler growth windows to avoid hard caps

sanjay: also add a telemetry alert for control-heartbeat-lag > 30s and tokenbucket-reject-rate > 5% simultaneous.

oncall_lex: good. Any other concerns?

maria: one note — tokenbucket regen bump increased short-lived cost but prevented customer errors. We should add an autodisable that reverts regen after 15m unless explicitly extended.

ryan: agree. I'll open a PR for an emergency-revert timeout on ratepolicy patches.

pm_zoe: CS notified and monitoring shared to customers.

oncall_lex: final status: mitigations in place, autoscaler healthy, queue draining, fallback routing active. ETA: 25m to full normalization. I'll file incident ticket after shift: INVEST-1812468000.

lisa: :thumbsup: nice triage everyone.

deploy-bot: rollout complete to hosted-gpu-1.

incident-bot: Incident 1812468000 status: mitigated — monitoring. Follow-up: postmortem assigned to sanjay/maria/ops_nick.

sanjay: starting postmortem notes now; will include timeline, root cause (control RPC deprioritization + tier capacity limit + tokenbucket regen config), mitigations, and action owners.

oncall_lex: handing back to normal ops, I'll update rotation channel when fully closed.

lisa: closing thread when metrics are stable. Final note: add runbook step to avoid applying large tokenbucket increases without control-priority check.

-- end of thread --
